title: Catch a squash after the fact, since the flag cannot be read
description:
repo-settings.sh --check cannot read allow_squash_merge from a safely-scoped CI token: GitHub's docs say merge-related settings need contents:read AND contents:write, so a token that could check them could also push code. That is not a trade worth making for a drift check, and the current 'this token cannot read the merge methods' line should say so as a deliberate limit rather than a missing permission.

Merge commits are already covered -- required_linear_history blocks them and that IS readable. The gap is squash merge: re-enabled, it would flatten a batch into one commit, which is what this workflow exists to prevent, and nothing would notice.

It is detectable after the fact with no extra permission: run check-batch.sh over main's recent commits in the weekly job. A squashed batch shows up as one commit closing several issues, which is exactly what that script refuses. Detection the Monday after beats never.

Also worth saying in DEVELOPERS.md that the merge-method half is unreadable by design, so nobody grants a write-scoped token chasing it. I told the maintainer to add Contents: Read-only before checking the docs; it does nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The weekly job refuses a commit on main that closes more than one issue, and DEVELOPERS.md says why the merge flags are not checked.
close_reason: The weekly job asks whether any recent commit on main closes more than one issue, which is what a squashed batch looks like once landed.

title: Batch: the scanner and the retired row
description: Five product issues: three in the scanning path and two in the catalogue API. Chosen to sit in disjoint files, as a test of whether autosquash conflict cost is driven by bead count or by file overlap.
close_reason: Landed.

title: Batch: the workflow's remaining edges
description: Five issues left over from the pull-request workflow: the checker that models three subject prefixes instead of the operation, the settings check nothing runs, a trailer block git cannot parse, a template asking for facts the machinery owns, and CI job names describing what those jobs used to do.
close_reason: Landed.

title: Batch: the checkers, tidied
description: Five issues raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1, all in the guardrail scripts that batch introduced. They ship together because four of them touch check-docs.sh or the suites around it, and landing them separately would mean rewriting the same files three times.
close_reason: Landed.

title: Make the trailer block one git can parse
description:
Every commit landed by the pull-request-workflow batch carries a Closes trailer, and 'git log --format=%(trailers:key=Closes)' prints nothing for all ten. Git wants the trailer block to be the final paragraph with nothing but trailers in it; several of these messages have a closing sentence after the body, so git reads the whole tail as prose.

grep and check-commit.sh both find them, so nothing is broken today. But %(trailers) is what GitHub and most tooling read to link a commit to an issue, and a trailer only a bespoke script can see is half a trailer.

check-commit.sh should require the trailers to be the last paragraph, and say so when they are not.
acceptance_criteria: git log --format='%(trailers:key=Closes,valueonly=true)' names the issue for every new commit, and check-commit.sh refuses a message where a paragraph follows the trailers.
close_reason: The trailer takes a colon, which is what git parses. GitHub accepts it for closing keywords too, so one form serves both.

title: Resolve a range the way autosquash would
description:
check-batch.sh models three literal subject prefixes rather than the operation they denote: fixup! and squash! are counted and refused, amend! is an explicit bail-out telling the contributor to use a different git feature.

Two costs. A pending fixup is a merge-readiness state, not a defect, but it turns the required check the same red as 'this commit holds two issues' -- for the whole review phase, since the documented workflow is fix, --fixup, push for every finding. And amend! is refused rather than handled.

Resolving the range as rebase --autosquash would -- mapping each fixup!/squash!/amend! to its target and checking the resolved set -- makes amend! stop being a special case by construction, and turns three prefix rules into one message.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1.
close_reason: fixup, squash and amend all resolve to the commit they name, so amend! stops being unreadable; a draft may carry them without failing.

title: Read script headers for duplicated prose too
description:
check-docs.sh globs *.md only. Two-thirds of the prose added by the pull-request-workflow batch was in shell and Python header comments, where it restated DEVELOPERS.md and ADR 0017 -- and the batch passed the checker clean.

Extend the input set to the comment blocks of scripts/*.sh and *.py. Expect it to fail on existing headers, which is the point: a script header should say what it enforces and where the rule lives, not re-derive the reasoning.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1.
close_reason: check-docs.sh reads the comments and docstrings of scripts/ as well as Markdown. Application code is inventory-tng-lwe.

title: The checkers share one voice and one harness
description:
check-commit.sh, check-batch.sh and repo-settings.sh each define fail/note and a verdict footer; the four .test.sh suites each copy an expect/scene harness, counters and summary. Roughly 70 duplicated lines, and it has already diverged: check-commit.test.sh grew a flag loop the three later copies cannot do, and two cases hand-roll expect because it is not parameterised by the command.

check-batch.sh also parses the trailer grammar itself while delegating the same rules to check-commit.sh, so ^(Closes|Refs) and the definition of 'the issue a commit names' exist in two implementations. The fix is for check-commit.sh --message-only to print a machine-readable answer that check-batch.sh consumes.

The glyph is load-bearing across a file boundary -- check-batch.sh greps check-commit.sh's output for a literal U+2717 -- while being redefined in each file.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1.
close_reason: report.sh holds fail, note, verdict and the trailer grammar; testlib.sh holds the harness. Four suites and three scripts source them instead of copying.

title: Let the message rules be checked on their own
description:
check-batch.sh runs check-commit.sh over each landed commit and then filters its objections by looking for the words 'staged' and 'tracker', because a landed commit has no staged diff for the tracker cross-check to read. The filter discards any objection whose text happens to use those words, including ones that do not exist yet.

Neither script can fix this alone: check-batch.sh cannot tell which objections are about staging without check-commit.sh saying so, and check-commit.sh has no reason to know it is being called over history. Raised by the review of pull request 1 as a finding belonging to no single issue.
acceptance_criteria: check-commit.sh can be asked for the message rules alone, and check-batch.sh asks for that instead of filtering prose.
close_reason: check-commit.sh takes --message-only for a caller reading landed history; check-batch.sh asks for it instead of discarding objections whose wording mentioned staging.

title: Enforce the batch rules in CI
description: New history job running check-batch.sh over the pull request range, with fetch-depth 0. Extend the docs job with check-docs.sh alongside lychee. Rewrite the comment on commit-check that explains why it does not read pull request history: that reasoning depends on squash merge, which this batch removes.
close_reason: A history job runs check-batch.sh over the pull request range; the docs job gained check-docs.sh; the commit-check job runs all three checker suites.

title: Fail the build on duplicated prose
description: New scripts/check-docs.sh: normalise Markdown, shingle into n-grams, flag any that appears in two files, with an allowlist for intentional repeats. Makes the one-topic-one-place rule a gate instead of a judgement. python3 stdlib only; jscpd was considered and rejected as too noisy on Markdown.
close_reason: check-docs.sh compares prose across Markdown files and refuses a passage that lives in two. Nine cases, most of them about what it must leave alone.

title: A failed decoder download is remembered forever, so the scanner never recovers
acceptance_criteria: A rejected decoder load is not remembered: a second loadDetector() after a failure attempts the import again, and a successful load is still kept for the life of the page. Tested in decoder.test.ts.
close_reason: A rejected load is forgotten, so the next scan starts over instead of replaying the first failure forever.

title: Prove the camera path decodes, with a fake video device
description:
CameraScanner.tsx lines 135-182 and 192 are the only place in this codebase where both test suites can be green and the product broken. They are everything after getUserMedia resolves: assigning the stream, play(), loadDetector(), the 5 Hz decode loop, and the teardown. jsdom has no camera, no video pipeline and no WebAssembly runtime, so vitest cannot reach them, and the component was deliberately kept to wiring so that everything decidable lives in frame.ts, cameras.ts, confirm.ts and decoder.ts, which are covered.

The specific risk, raised by a review of inventory-tng-suv and still open: if the ImageData handoff into the decoder were wrong -- a detached buffer, a tainted canvas, the wrong pixel format -- the scanner would decode nothing at a shelf while every test passed. Nothing exercises the real decode today. The integration spec from inventory-tng-8o2 opens a camera but only asserts where the binary was fetched from; it never decodes.

APPROACH

Chromium accepts --use-file-for-fake-video-capture=<path>.y4m alongside the --use-fake-device-for-media-stream and --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream flags decoder-origin.spec.ts already sets. It feeds the file to getUserMedia in place of a lens, so the real pipeline runs end to end: real stream, real play(), real frame grab, real WASM decode, real cart line.

Generate the stream at test time; do not commit it. Y4M holds uncompressed frames, so even a couple of seconds at 640x480 is several megabytes, and a committed fixture would also go stale against whatever the label generator produces next.

ffmpeg in a container is fine and consistent with the project, which already lists a container runtime as a prerequisite for PostgreSQL.

PODMAN IS THE PREFERRED RUNTIME, so write the helper for Podman and let Docker be the substitute rather than the other way round. Two things to settle rather than assume:
  - Rootless Podman and bind mounts. The container has to write the y4m somewhere the Chromium process on the host can read. Under rootless Podman a bind-mounted path is written as a different uid than the host user unless :U or --userns=keep-id is used, so a naive "-v out:/out" can produce a file the test cannot open. Settle this first; it is the most likely thing to go wrong.
  - CI's integration job uses GitHub Actions service containers, not arbitrary container runs. Confirm a plain container run is available on the runner, and say what happens if it is not. DEVELOPERS.md's prerequisite table and the Podman note beneath it are the canonical place to record whatever is decided.

WORTH CONSIDERING: get the QR from the project rather than inventing one. Playwright can open /api/labels/sheet for a code minted by the test, screenshot the rendered symbol, and hand that PNG to ffmpeg. The test then proves mint -> print -> scan against the project's own ECC-Q output at its own module size, which is a far better assertion than a synthetic QR and exercises inventory-tng-n2o's work as well.

CONSTRAINTS ON THE CLIP
  - frame.ts downscales to 640 on the long edge before decoding, so the symbol has to survive that.
  - The decode loop runs at 5 Hz and the cart debounces repeats, so the code must be held in frame long enough to be caught at least once.
  - Chromium only. The project already runs a single Chromium project, so this costs nothing.
  - Headless behaviour of the file variant is unverified. The fake device itself works headless here (decoder-origin.spec.ts passes), but that is the pattern generator, not the file reader.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: moving the vitest coverage number. Coverage comes from vitest run --coverage over src/**, and playwright.config.ts states that the integration suite has no part in the coverage threshold. Making a Playwright run count would mean collecting V8 coverage over CDP, mapping it through source maps and merging it with vitest's report -- a separate piece of work and a change to what the threshold means. This bead is about the risk, not the number, and the number will not move.

Raised from a question about why frontend coverage sits below the backend's.
acceptance_criteria: A Playwright test drives a real getUserMedia stream carrying a QR code and asserts a cart line appears with the right item and quantity. The stream is generated during the run, not committed. The generator works under Podman for whoever runs the suite, locally and in CI, with Docker as the substitute -- or the bead records why it cannot and what was done instead.
notes:
REVIEWED AFTER inventory-tng-w1e LANDED (commit e4387a7). What that bead actually changed here:

THE SCOPE DID NARROW, AND MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL NOTE EXPECTED. CameraScanner.tsx is at 100% and the frontend at 98.85% lines. Covered in vitest now, so NOT this bead's to assert: the stream reaching the preview before play, every track stopped on teardown, a stream or a decoder arriving after teardown being released, the second enumeration and a device that refuses it, an aborted lens switch staying silent, a code reaching the newest onCode without reopening the camera, and the whole decode loop -- busy-skipping, the post-await recheck, a refusal read as no-code -- which now lives in frontend/src/scan/decodeLoop.ts with its own tests.

THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION IS NOW WRONG IN ONE PLACE. It says lines 135-182 and 192 are the only place both suites can be green and the product broken. Those lines are covered; what is left uncovered is narrower and is exactly the original risk sentence: the ImageData handoff. Whether what frame.ts produces is something zxing can actually read is still asserted nowhere.

THAT RISK MOVED SLIGHTLY. frame.ts's contract changed: the grabber now answers with the video element itself where there is no 2D context, instead of null with the fallback written in the component. So both ways into the decoder -- bounded ImageData, or the element -- are now decided in frame.ts, and a real browser takes the first one. A Playwright test is the only thing that can tell them apart.

A DOC OBLIGATION WAS CREATED. w1e recorded this gap in two places that must be updated when this bead lands, or they will be lying: DEVELOPERS.md 'Integration tests' now has a paragraph beginning 'Nothing anywhere decodes a QR code' which names this bead, and frontend/src/scan/testFixtures.ts's header says no suite claims it. Both are acceptance criteria for this bead, not follow-ups.

STILL TRUE AND STILL CONSTRAINTS: frame.ts bounds the long edge at 640 (WORKING_EDGE) so the symbol has to survive that; the loop runs at DECODE_INTERVAL_MS = 200ms and the cart debounces repeats, so the code has to be held in frame; Chromium only. decoder-origin.spec.ts remains the nearest thing and still decodes nothing -- it says so itself.
close_reason:
A Playwright test now drives a real getUserMedia stream carrying one of this project's own ECC-Q symbols and asserts the cart line: frontend/integration/decodes.spec.ts, with the clip built in frontend/integration/qrVideo.ts.

IT FOUND THE BUG IT WAS WRITTEN FOR, on its first run. The symbol carries the deep link (decision 0011 section 3), so the camera decodes HTTPS://INVENTORY.NYCMESH.NET/S/<code> -- and the app sent that whole string to GET /api/labels/{code}, which 404s. The in-app camera had never once worked against this project's own stickers, and neither suite could see it: every unit test feeds the scanner a bare code. Fixed by codeFromScan in frontend/src/scan/deepLink.ts, applied at the one funnel every scanned code passes through (useScannedCode), so a wedge scanner gun -- which reads the same symbol and types the same URL -- is fixed with it. Decision 0011 section 3 now records the obligation as well as the benefit, which is the gap that let this ship.

ON PODMAN AND ffmpeg, which the acceptance criteria asked to be settled: neither is needed, so neither question arises. Y4M is uncompressed frames behind a one-line header, so the clip is written directly in Node -- no container runtime, no rootless bind-mount uid problem, and nothing for a GitHub Actions runner to provide beyond the browser it already installs. The symbol is not invented either: the matrix comes from inventory.labels.symbol_for, so it is the project's own output at its own error correction level. One 640x480 frame, generated per run and deleted after, never committed.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: the printed sticker's own readability, which the backend suite already asserts by decoding what segno drew with zxing-cpp. This test owns the handoff in between -- the ImageData frame.ts hands the decoder -- which was the risk in the description.

Verified non-vacuous: blank the film and the test fails.

Docs updated in the same change, as w1e's note required: DEVELOPERS.md 'Integration tests', frontend/src/scan/testFixtures.ts, the react-frontend skill (npm test does not run this suite), and decision 0011.

title: DECISION: what occurred_at should be for a batch saved long after it was filled
description:
frontend/src/batch/movements.ts does not send occurred_at, so every batch is recorded as having happened when Save was pressed. The cart already mints and persists createdAt when it opens (frontend/src/cart/cartState.ts) and nothing reads it, so the information exists and is being thrown away.

Decision 0011 section 6 lists occurred_at in the POST body. StockTransaction.occurred_at is the ledger's default ordering key and the ledger is append-only, so a batch recorded at the wrong time cannot be corrected -- only compensated.

The case that makes this a decision rather than a fix: a volunteer fills a cart at a shelf with no signal and saves at the door two hours later, which argues for createdAt. But a cart left open overnight, or restored from localStorage days later, would then be recorded as having happened when it was opened, which is worse -- and StockTransactionCreateSerializer refuses anything more than CLOCK_SKEW in the future but nothing in the past.

Options: send createdAt always; send it only when it is within some window of now and fall back to the server clock otherwise; ask the volunteer when a cart is older than some age; or keep the current behaviour and record why, deleting createdAt as dead state.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-vci.
acceptance_criteria: A batch's occurred_at is the time the decision says it should be, and cart.createdAt is either used or removed. If the answer is 'Save time', a decision record says so.
close_reason: Decision 0018: the server's clock decides occurred_at and the client sends none; cart.createdAt removed rather than left unread.

title: Nothing prefetches the label map, so every scan is two live round trips
description:
Decision 0011 section 6 says the client keeps the label map and the catalogue, so a scan resolves without a network round trip. LabelListView's own docstring says the same: 'Unpaginated, deliberately. This exists to be fetched once and cached, so that a scan resolves without a round trip from a basement.'

Nothing fetches /api/labels at all. frontend/src/scan/applyCode.ts issues GET /api/labels/{code} and then GET /api/items/{id} for every code, live. Twenty-four scans in a basement is forty-eight requests, on the connection decision 0011 section 1 says is the reason the whole batch design exists.

The unpaginated endpoint built for this is currently dead weight.

What is needed: fetch /api/labels and /api/items once when the app opens, keep them (the same localStorage discipline as the cart and the remembered volunteer, in frontend/src/storage.ts), resolve a scanned code against them, and fall back to the live read when a code is not in the cached map -- a label minted since the cache was filled. Worth deciding at the same time how the cache is refreshed and how stale it is allowed to get, since a wrong item name in a cart line is worse than a slow scan.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-p3t and inventory-tng-ea6.
acceptance_criteria: A scan of a code the client has already seen adds a cart line with no network request. A code minted since the last refresh still resolves. The staleness rule is written down.
close_reason: The label map and catalogue are fetched once on open and kept; a scan resolves against them with no request, falling back live for a code they do not hold.

title: An administrator cannot find a retired row through the API
description:
DetailView (backend/src/inventory/views.py) lets an administrator read and repair a row the pick-list has withdrawn -- a retired item or location, a merged volunteer -- but only if they already know its id. Every list endpoint still serves OFFERED_* to everybody, so there is no way to arrive at that id.

test_catalogue_writes.py::test_retiring_an_item_takes_it_out_of_the_pick_list shows the shape: the administrator retires an item and their own list immediately reads []. Undoing it is then possible only through the Django admin, which decision 0014 point 4 reserves for 'a broken deployment, three in the morning' -- not for routine repair. That directly undercuts point 1 of the same decision: 'the item list gains editing, in place, where the thing already is'.

Volunteers escape it by accident: the 409 body from decision 0015 hands the client the pk of the record to look at.

Options: lift the is_administrator swap out of DetailView into a mixin the list views share; or add an 'active' filter parameter that only an administrator may set; or a separate withdrawn-rows collection. The first changes what an administrator's pick-list shows, which is wrong for the cart -- so the second is probably right, and it needs deciding rather than guessing.

Note this is NOT inventory-tng-6c7, which asks what active=False means for stock physically on a shelf. This asks whether an administrator can find the row at all.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-0rr.
acceptance_criteria: An administrator can reach a retired item, a retired location and a merged volunteer through the API without knowing an id in advance, or a decision records why the Django admin is the path for that.
close_reason: ?withdrawn=true lists what a collection took out of its list, for administrators only, leaving the pick-list unchanged.

title: Retiring or merging a volunteer leaves their custody location behind
description:
LocationSerializer.validate_held_by refuses a NEW custody location for a merged or retired volunteer, on the grounds that it would be 'the second generation of the duplicate the merge existed to remove'. Nothing does anything about the custody location a duplicate already holds, and the volunteer endpoint can create that state two ways.

Both confirmed against a running server, with a volunteer_custody Location held by Sean:

- PATCH /api/volunteers/{sean} {"merged_into": {other}} -> 200. Sean's custody location stays active, named after Sean, and offered in the location pick-list.
- PATCH /api/volunteers/{sean} {"active": false} -> 200. Same outcome by the other route.

So the guard is placed where it was cheap rather than where the state is created, and the serializers.py module docstring's rule 3 is only half true -- it has been narrowed to say so.

The fix has to be decided rather than assumed. Repointing the location at the survivor is the obvious move for a merge, but location_one_custody_per_volunteer makes it fail when the survivor already holds one, which is the common case for a real duplicate. The alternatives are retiring the duplicate's location, or refusing the operation while one exists and saying what to do first. Retirement has no obvious answer for the stock still recorded there, which is inventory-tng-6c7's question.

The location cannot simply be deleted: the ledger refers to it.

Raised by two reviews of inventory-tng-0rr.
acceptance_criteria: After a merge or a retirement, no active custody location names the affected record -- or the operation is refused with a body that says what to do first. Tested through the API for both operations, and for the survivor-has-one and survivor-has-none cases.
close_reason: Merging or retiring somebody who holds an active custody location is refused, naming it, rather than leaving it pointing at a withdrawn record.

title: A test that every model is registered in the Django admin
description:
Decision 0014 point 4 keeps the Django admin as the fallback that still works when the single-page app does not -- a broken deployment, a model with no bespoke interface yet, a correction somebody needs to make at three in the morning.

That is only true if it stays complete. Its currency is nearly free, since registering a model is three lines, so the obligation is small and worth enforcing rather than promising: a test asserting that every concrete model in the inventory app is registered turns 'kept up to date as the models evolve' into a build failure.

This is the repo's own pattern -- enforce the invariant where the mistake is made rather than describe it where it might be read.
acceptance_criteria: A new model added without registering it in admin.py fails the test run, with a message naming the model.
close_reason: Implemented in parallel worktrees, then reviewed and simplified once over the merged diff

title: Administrative powers in the volunteer app, with step-up before anything destructive
description:
Decision 0014. Signing in does not navigate anywhere else: the item list gains editing, the volunteer picker gains merging, a label gains revocation, in place where the thing already is.

Depends on the catalogue write API and on GET /api/me.

Decision 0014 point 5 is part of this and not a follow-up: merging volunteers, revoking labels and editing the catalogue prompt for the password or second factor again even inside a valid session. This is the mitigation for the consequence the decision records -- putting administrative capability in the same application means script injected into it reaches the destructive operations too. Appending to the ledger is deliberately not affected, because it is what an administrator does most often.

A strict Content-Security-Policy is a requirement of this work for the same reason.
acceptance_criteria: An administrator edits the catalogue without leaving the app; destructive operations require re-authentication; appending a batch does not; a CSP is in place and tested; a volunteer sees no administrative controls and is refused server-side if they call the endpoints anyway.
close_reason: Closed

title: The integration seed is guarded by DEBUG, which a cluster can legitimately set
description:
seed_integration_data creates a Django superuser whose password is written down in this repository, guarded by settings.DEBUG. The command ships inside the backend image, and django.debug is a Helm value -- so a cluster running with DJANGO_DEBUG=true is one kubectl exec away from a known-password superuser against real data.

DEBUG being on in a deployed environment is already a serious misconfiguration, so this is a second lock on a door that should not be open. But it is the wrong lock: DEBUG means 'this is a development server', not 'it is safe to create a published credential here'. An explicit --i-know-what-this-does flag, or a dedicated environment variable, says what it means.

Separately: the filter().delete() followed by create_superuser is not wrapped in a transaction, so a failure between them leaves no integration login at all and the next Playwright run fails at the login form rather than at the seed.

Found by a review of inventory-tng-hd0.
acceptance_criteria: Creating the seeded superuser requires an explicit acknowledgement rather than DEBUG alone, and the delete-then-create is atomic.
close_reason: Implemented in parallel worktrees, then reviewed and simplified once over the merged diff

title: A merged volunteer's email is a dead end for the person re-registering
description:
POST /api/volunteers rejects a duplicate email through DRF's UniqueValidator, whose queryset is every Volunteer row. Search and listing go through Volunteer.objects.selectable(), which excludes merged and inactive records.

So: Sean's duplicate record is merged into Sean McGinnis and keeps sean@example.org. A new Sean searches the pick-list, is offered nothing that matches, and self-registers with his own address. He gets 400 'volunteer with this email already exists' naming a record the API refuses to show him. There is no way forward from that screen -- and self-registration after a failed search is the single flow this endpoint exists to serve.

Options, none obviously right: search could include merged records and offer to point at the survivor; the uniqueness check could be scoped to selectable rows (two rows then share an address, which the partial index permits since it is not unique-per-anything); or the error could name the merge and offer the surviving volunteer as a choice. The third is the best experience and the most work.

Found by a review of inventory-tng-hd0.
acceptance_criteria: A volunteer whose address is held by a merged or inactive record can complete registration, or is shown the record that holds it. Tested through the API.
close_reason: Closed

title: A batch kind constrains which sides are required but not which are forbidden
description:
KIND_REQUIRES in backend/src/inventory/views.py checks only that each movement carries the sides its kind requires. It never checks that a movement omits the side its kind excludes.

So kind=receipt with a from_location is accepted: a receipt means stock arriving from outside the system, yet the line drains a known location, and 201 is returned. Same for consumption with a to_location. The ledger is append-only, so the balance view stays wrong until somebody notices and posts a compensating movement.

Completing the rule: checkout and consumption forbid nothing extra (a checkout may name where it went); receipt forbids from_location; consumption forbids to_location (stock fitted at an install has left the system); transfer requires both and forbids neither. The 409 body already reports offending lines by index, so the shape needs no change.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-hgm. Decision 0011 section 6 states the required-sides half and should state this half too.
acceptance_criteria: A receipt carrying a from_location, and a consumption carrying a to_location, are both 409 with the offending line index. Decision 0011 section 6 states which sides each kind forbids. Tests cover both.
close_reason: Idempotency scoped to (actor, idempotency_key) with a migration; kind now constrains forbidden sides as well as required ones; both recorded in decision 0011

title: The /api index cannot advertise a write-only endpoint
description:
views.py states the invariant 'an endpoint cannot be advertised without being described, or described without being advertised', and DEVELOPERS.md tells clients to discover the API by fetching /api and following the links. POST /api/stock/transactions -- the endpoint the project exists for -- is in neither, because test_api_root_links_actually_resolve GETs every advertised link and asserts 200, which a POST-only endpoint cannot satisfy.

So the index's contract is really 'GET this and it resolves', not 'here is the API'. Either the index carries a method alongside each link and the test follows suit, or discovery is declared to be the OpenAPI schema's job and the claim in views.py and DEVELOPERS.md is corrected to match. Raised while implementing inventory-tng-hgm.
acceptance_criteria: A client following the documented discovery path can find every endpoint, or the documentation no longer claims they can. views.py's ENDPOINTS comment matches whatever is decided.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enforce TLS at the Helm chart rather than in prose
description:
Raised by the /simplify altitude pass on ADR 0011.

ADR 0011 establishes that TLS is a FUNCTIONAL requirement, not only a security one: without a secure context navigator.mediaDevices is undefined and QR scanning disappears silently. But infra/helm/inventory-tng still exposes ingress.tls.enabled as a toggle, templates/ingress.yaml simply branches on it, and there is no values.schema.json. So the only thing between an operator and a scanner-less install is a paragraph in docs/deployment.md.

The repo's own pattern is to enforce invariants where the mistake is made rather than describe them where they might be read. Either render TLS unconditionally, or fail the template when it is disabled.
acceptance_criteria: A chart rendered with TLS disabled either fails or still produces a TLS-terminating ingress. Verified with helm template.
close_reason: TLS is no longer a chart toggle and rendering without a certificate fails; batch validation now resolves each distinct id once, taking a 24-line cart from 81 queries to 12

title: DECISION: which of Item.reorder_quantity and VendorOffer.units_per_order is authoritative
description:
Flagged while designing 0011 and deliberately not resolved there.

Item.reorder_quantity and VendorOffer.units_per_order already overlap and it is unclear which is authoritative or what unit each is expressed in. If a vendor sells zip ties 100 to a bag and units_per_order is 100, does a reorder_quantity of 2 mean two bags or two ties? The sheet stores one 'units per order' value as the string '100 ft', which is where the confusion comes from.

Adding Label.quantity does not make this worse - it describes how stock is HANDLED, not how it is bought or reordered - but it does add a third quantity-ish field and makes the ambiguity harder to keep ignoring. The low-stock alerting volunteers asked for depends on getting this right.
acceptance_criteria: It is written down which field is authoritative for reorder decisions and in what unit each is expressed; docs/data-model.md says so; an ADR records it if the answer is not obvious from the field names.

title: Label code minting and the printable label generator
description:
Decision 0011 sections 5 and 7. 'Half the QR codes don't scan' is a printing failure and no library choice fixes it.

Mint codes from Crockford Base32 (digits and uppercase letters excluding I, L, O, U), 10 characters. Encode the payload uppercase - HTTPS://INVENTORY.NYCMESH.NET/S/7QK3M2XV9A - so the encoder can use QR alphanumeric mode, which packs two characters per 11 bits instead of 8 bits each.

Generated labels must carry: error correction level Q (not the L or M most generators default to), a specified minimum module size and quiet zone, the code in human-readable text underneath so a dead QR is still a working label, and the print date so an aged batch can be replaced as a set.

Confirm the ECC percentage and the resulting QR version against ISO/IEC 18004 - the ADR's figures come from secondary sources.
acceptance_criteria: Codes mint from the stated alphabet and are unique; a printable sheet renders at ECC Q with human-readable code and print date; label revoke-and-reprint works without touching item identity.
notes: Minting and the printable sheet are built and tested. One thing is NOT true yet and matters before anybody prints for real: every sticker encodes LABEL_BASE_URL/S/{code}, and nothing routes /S/ — that is inventory-tng-ea6, raised to P1 for this reason. A label is a permanent physical object, so a batch printed before ea6 lands is stuck pointing at a URL that does nothing. Raised by a review of this bead.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fail CI when models and migrations disagree
description:
Raised by the xhigh code review of the data-model work. CI runs lint, format, type check and tests, but nothing runs 'makemigrations --check --dry-run'. A model change committed without its migration passes CI unless a test happens to exercise the drifted field, and then fails at deploy time when migrate runs against a real database.

This matters more than usual here: the data model landed ~800 lines of migrations including hand-written RunSQL for the balance view and the append-only triggers.
acceptance_criteria: CI fails when a model change has no accompanying migration. Verified by removing a migration locally and seeing the check fail.
notes: Corrected during /simplify: the check was initially added as a CI-only step, which breaks the repo's local-equals-CI principle (ADR 0007, and the same principle ADR 0010 relies on for the schema gate). It is now backend/src/inventory/tests/test_migrations.py, so 'uv run pytest' catches drift locally and CI needs no special step. Verified failing and passing.
close_reason: Added a 'Migrations match the models' step to the backend CI job running makemigrations --check --dry-run. Verified both directions by adding a field with no migration (exit 1, CI would fail) and reverting (exit 0). Noted in the django-backend skill next to the existing migration guidance.

title: Migrate data from the Google Sheets inventory
description:
Import the existing Google Forms/Sheets inventory. Measured from the actual export, NOT the 15k+ originally assumed: 52 catalogued items and 3,439 usable submissions (Jul 2022 - Aug 2026).

Real work is data cleaning, not volume. See docs/data-model.md#migrating-the-existing-sheet for the work. Each rule and the figures it produces are in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md, and are not restated here: the brief's figures come from 'manage.py profile_sheet' over the workbook, a test checks the brief against what that command emits, and a copy in this description would be the one thing in the chain nothing checks. Four of the six rules are code in inventory/sheet/ and can be called directly.

What the importer has to do with each:

- Item strings, section 1. Every string that does not resolve mints an ItemIdentifier. items.resolve() answers per string with how it resolved and, when it did not, why -- an ambiguous string, one the catalogue does not hold, or a retired NYCM code. Unresolvable is an answer and must import as one rather than be guessed at; the report's 'neither resolved nor accounted for' line is expected to stay at zero.
- Corrections, section 2. Settled: a note naming the record and an act of adjusting it. corrections.is_correction() decides, and those rows import as adjustment rather than as volunteer activity.
- Locations, section 3. locations.locations() yields candidates, not locations. They are a seed for inventory-tng-o5t and must not be imported before that bead has been to the meeting. "a volunteer's home" is not a Location row at all: location_held_by_iff_custody wants a holder, so the importer pairs it with the person rule 6 resolves.
- Job references, section 4. jobs.job_reference() gives the string StockTransaction.job_reference holds. One note names two jobs and the field takes the first.
- Batching, section 5, and volunteers, section 6, are not settled: inventory-tng-a82 and inventory-tng-5r2. Anything genuinely ambiguous imports flagged rather than silently merged.

Timestamps arrive naive and occasionally absent -- Submission.at says why -- so the importer decides the zone and what a row with no timestamp does, and records both.

Keep each raw source row as JSONB for provenance so the import is re-runnable. django-import-export is likely overkill here; a management command is probably enough.
notes: Packaging ambiguity found while designing 0011: many items are counted individually but handled in packets, and historical quantities are recorded in BOTH units by different volunteers. Zip Ties Reusable (stock 600, packs of 100) shows 1 x30, 100 x17, 200 x9, 2 x5, 400 x2, 5 x2 - so a recorded '1' is either one tie or one packet and only a volunteer who was there can say which. The migration must not guess a multiplier: import the value literally and flag the item for a physical count. See decision 0011 section 6 and its Questions for the project owner #3.

title: Add LICENSE
description: MeshDB carries a LICENSE file. Pick a license consistent with NYC Mesh practice and add it before the repo goes public.
close_reason: MIT LICENSE added at the repository root. Verified the body matches the SPDX MIT text exactly after whitespace/case normalisation, which is what GitHub's licensee uses to report the license on the repo main page, and confirmed the file is not gitignored. License also declared as an SPDX expression in backend/pyproject.toml and frontend/package.json, and linked from README. Deliberately no license-files entry in pyproject: ../LICENSE sits outside the project directory and build backends reject that; the text lives once, at the root.

title: Integrate GitHub issues with beads
description: Volunteers work in GitHub issues; agents work in beads. Wire bd config github.org/github.repo so agents are aware of GitHub issues and can open them. Requires the nycmeshnet/inventory-tng remote to exist.
notes:
Precondition checked 2026-08-21 and unmet: 'gh repo view nycmeshnet/inventory-tng' resolves to no repository, and the only remote here is lotia/nycmesh-inventory-tng. Wiring bd's github.org and github.repo at an organisation repository that does not exist would point agents at a 404.

Deferred rather than closed, because the work is still wanted and the description still describes it. Deferred rather than left open, because an open bead with no blocker sits in 'bd ready' claiming to be startable, and this one is not: nothing a contributor does in this repository unblocks it. The thing that does is somebody creating the repository under the nycmeshnet organisation, which is a decision for NYC Mesh rather than a task.

Re-check by re-running the command above.

title: Add ADRs for deliberate divergences from MeshDB
description: docs/decisions/: monorepo choice, Vite SPA over meshforms (bitrotted: Next 14/React 18/MUI 5/TS 5.3 vs current 16/19/9/7, plus direct-to-Postgres client), ruff over black+isort+flake8, psycopg3 over psycopg2, Django 6.1 over 5.2 LTS.

description: Replace standalone CLAUDE.md with a symlink; add CODEX.md and GEMINI.md symlinks. Resolves the beads warning about AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md not sharing an inode.

title: Write DEVELOPERS.md for contributor setup and workflow
description: Toolchain (mise/uv/python 3.14), first-time setup, devcontainer workflow, repo layout including the backend/inventory_tng nesting gotcha, common tasks (deps, migrations, tests, new apps), bd pointer, branch/commit conventions.
close_reason: Closed
